stories.headline: Orbán-linked oligarchs accused of moving billions abroad as new government prepares accountability drive
stories.summary: Incoming PM Magyar publicly alleged that Fidesz-connected oligarchs — including the Mészáros family — are transferring tens of billions of forints to the UAE, US, Uruguay and other non-extradition countries, and selling media assets (TV2, Lounge Event Kft.) at below-market prices. Magyar called on the NAV and police to freeze transactions; the NAV confirmed it had suspended several high-value transfers on money-laundering suspicion. Named companies denied being for sale.

stories.headline: Orbán resigns parliamentary seat to lead Fidesz reconstruction; multiple senior figures also step back
stories.summary: Outgoing PM Viktor Orbán announced on April 25 he will not take up his parliamentary mandate, ending his 36-year continuous presence in the legislature, and will instead focus on 'renewing the national side' as Fidesz chairman; Gergely Gulyás was named to lead the sharply reduced parliamentary faction. Multiple senior figures including Deputy PM Semjén Zsolt, party vice-president Kósa Lajos, and regional director Bánki Erik also announced they would not take seats, while Mi Hazánk leader Toroczkai commented pointedly. Investigative journalists and opposition politicians (including Hadházy) raised questions about Orbán's legal accountability and potential flight risk.

stories.headline: Magyar to meet von der Leyen in Brussels Wednesday to unfreeze up to €18bn in EU funds before August deadline
stories.summary: Incoming PM Magyar announced he will travel to Brussels on Wednesday April 29 for informal talks with European Commission President von der Leyen about releasing frozen EU funds; Hungary faces losing roughly €10bn in pandemic recovery money if it misses an August 31 deadline, with a further €18bn frozen over rule-of-law disputes. Prior working-level meetings took place in Budapest (April 18–19) and Brussels (Saturday). Fidesz-aligned commentators disputed whether Magyar had actually secured a suspension of the €1m/day migration fine.

stories.headline: EU unblocks €90bn Ukraine loan after Hungary drops veto following Druzhba pipeline resumption
stories.summary: EU member states agreed to unblock the €90bn loan to Ukraine after Ukraine resumed pumping Russian oil through the Druzhba pipeline to Hungary and Slovakia, resolving the dispute that outgoing PM Orbán had used to block the loan since February. Magyar had publicly urged Zelenskyy to reopen the pipeline and confirmed Hungary would drop its veto once deliveries resumed; MOL reported oil deliveries restarting around April 22.

stories.headline: ECJ rules Hungary's anti-LGBTQ laws violate EU treaty values; new 24-hour LGBTQ TV channel applies for license
stories.summary: The European Court of Justice ruled on April 20 that Hungary's 2021 law banning LGBTQ content for minors violates EU fundamental rights, marking the first time the court found a member state breached EU Charter values. The ruling came nine days after Orbán's election defeat. Within days of the ruling, an anonymous Hungarian company applied for a media license to operate a 24-hour LGBTQ-themed online TV channel ('Szivárvány TV').

stories.headline: Magyar announces Tisza cabinet with 16 ministries; minister picks include Orbán Anita as FM, Vitézy as transport, Lannert as education
stories.summary: PM-elect Magyar announced his incoming cabinet in multiple waves: initial seven ministers named April 20 (including Anita Orbán as foreign minister and deputy PM, economist Kármán András as finance minister, and former HDF commander Ruszin-Szendi Romulusz as defence minister), followed by transport minister Vitézy Dávid, education minister Lannert Judit, and social minister Kátai-Németh Vilmos (Hungary's first blind minister). The 16-ministry structure dismantles Orbán's centralized model; Tisza's speaker nominee is Ágnes Forsthoffer.

stories.headline: Magyar demands President Sulyok's resignation; Fidesz launches petition drive to keep him in office
stories.summary: Since his April 12 election victory, Magyar has repeatedly demanded that President Sulyok resign as an 'Orbán puppet,' giving a May 31 deadline and warning the Tisza supermajority could force removal. Fidesz launched a CitizenGO petition that gathered over 75,000 signatures (including Orbán's own) urging Sulyok to stay. The Sándor Palace gave a non-committal response; a legal scholar argued Magyar himself may be constitutionally unswearable; and civil society organized a solidarity demonstration. Sulyok meantime signed last-minute decrees and announced the May 9 inaugural parliamentary session.

stories.headline: MNB scandal widens: former governor Simor alleges extortion by central bank vice-president; prosecution takes over investigation
stories.summary: Former National Bank governor András Simor alleged on ATV that an MNB vice-president (Kandrács Csaba) effectively blackmailed him in December 2023 into resigning from Erste Group's supervisory board, with Erste Bank Hungary confirming it had faced 'questionable treatment.' Current MNB governor Varga Mihály immediately launched an internal investigation; the Prosecutor General's office transferred the police investigation into the MNB and its foundations to the Central Investigation Prosecutor's Office. Former governor Matolcsy denied wrongdoing; further former bankers came forward with similar claims.
